extracted.intended_audience: users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (researchers / computational algebraists using SINGULAR libraries)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for SINGULAR library procedures (weierstr.lib, rootsmr.lib, rootsur.lib, gfan.lib) describing usage, assumptions, returns, and notes for each routine. Useful for programmers and mathematicians using these libraries to perform algebraic computations (Weierstrass division/preparation, root counting, Sturm sequences, convex geometry via gfan).

rubrics_metrics.name: weierstrDiv
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: weierstrDiv(g,f,d); g,f=poly, d=integer. Purpose: perform the Weierstrass division of g by f up to order d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: f must be general of finite order b in the last ring variable T; if not use lastvarGeneral first. Return: list l with l[1]*f + l[2] = g up to total degree d, deg_T(l[2]) < b, and l[3] the number of iterations; if f is not T-general return (0,g). Note: works for any monomial ordering. Theory: uses Grauert-Remmert proof. Example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: weierstrPrep
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: weierstrPrep(f,d); f=poly, d=integer. Purpose: perform the Weierstrass preparation of f up to order d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: f must be general of finite order b in the last ring variable T; if not apply lastvarGeneral first. Return: list l where l[1] is a unit, l[2] a Weierstrass polynomial (T^b + lower terms) and l[3] iterations number, satisfying l[1]*f = l[2] up to total degree d; if f not T-general return (0,0). Note: works for any monomial ordering. Theory: Grauert-Remmert. Example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: lastvarGeneral
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: lastvarGeneral(f,d); f=poly. Return: poly g obtained from f by a generic change of variables s.t. g is general of finite order b with respect to the last ring variable T (g(0,...,0,T)=c*T^b + higher terms, c!=0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: procedure works for any monomial ordering. Example shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: generalOrder
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: generalOrder(f); f=poly. Return: integer b if f is general of order b w.r.t. the last variable T, or -1 if not (i.e. f(0,...,0,T) has order b or equals 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: works for any monomial ordering. Example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: nrRootsProbab
rubrics_metrics.description: Return: int, the number of real roots of the ideal I by a probabilistic algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If I is not a Groebner basis, std will be used to compute one; if it already is one, it must be w.r.t. any global ordering. Parameter n (if <10) is number of digits used for constructing a random characteristic polynomial (default n=5); larger n is safer but slower. If printlevel>0 number of complex solutions is displayed. Provides a warning when pseudorandom numbers used and suggests verify(p,b,i) to check result. Example and notes about speed vs deterministic method.

rubrics_metrics.name: nrRootsDeterm
rubrics_metrics.description: Return: int, the number of real roots of the ideal I by a deterministic algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If I is not a Groebner basis, std will compute one; if it already is one it must be w.r.t. a global ordering. Note: printlevel>0 displays number of complex solutions; nrRootsProbab is usually faster. Examples given.

rubrics_metrics.name: symsignature
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: symsignature(m); m matrix (must be symmetric). Return: int, the signature of m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example included; see matbil for how matrix may be generated.

rubrics_metrics.name: sturmquery
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sturmquery(h,b,i); h poly, b,i ideal. Return: int, the Sturm query of h in V(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: i is a Groebner basis, b is an ordered monomial basis of r/i (r = basering). Example provided. See symsignature and matbil cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: matbil
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: matbil(h,b,i); h poly, b,i ideal. Return: matrix, the matrix of the bilinear form (f,g) |-> trace(m fhg), where m fhg = multiplication with fhg on r/i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: i is a Groebner basis and b is an ordered monomial basis of r/i (r = basering). Large example printed. See matmult and tracemult cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: matmult
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: matmult(f,b,i); f poly, b,i ideal. Return: matrix, the matrix of the multiplication map by f (m_f) on r/i w.r.t. basis b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: i is a Groebner basis and b is qbase(i). Example printed. See coords, matbil cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: tracemult
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: tracemult(f,B,I); f poly, B,I ideal. Return: number, the trace of the multiplication by f on r/I written in monomial basis B (faster than matmult + trace).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: I given by a Groebner basis and B ordered monomial basis of r/I. Example shows tracemult output and cross-references to matmult and trace.

rubrics_metrics.name: coords
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: coords(f,b,i), f poly, b,i ideal. Return: list of numbers, the coordinates of the class of f (mod i) in the monomial basis b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: i is a Groebner basis and b is an ordered monomial basis of r/i. Example demonstrates basis and resulting coordinates. See matbil/matmult cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: randcharpoly
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: randcharpoly(b,i); randcharpoly(b,i,n); b,i ideal; n int. Return: poly, the characteristic polynomial of a pseudorandom rational univariate projection having one zero per zero of i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: i is a Groebner basis and b an ordered monomial basis of r/i. If n<10, it gives number of digits used for pseudorandom coefficients (default n=5). Note: shows warning if printlevel>0 and suggests verify(p,b,i) to validate pseudorandom result. Example generating large polynomial and using nrroots on it.

rubrics_metrics.name: verify
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: verify(p,B,I); p poly, B,I ideal. Return: integer 1 iff polynomial p splits the points of V(I). Used to check randcharpoly result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: I given by Groebner basis and B ordered monomial basis of r/I. Note: prints result if printlevel>0. Example verifying a randcharpoly output.

rubrics_metrics.name: randlinpoly
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: randlinpoly(); randlinpoly(n); n int. Return: poly, linear combination of variables with pseudorandom coefficients (range digits controlled by n, default n=5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows returned linear polynomial. See randcharpoly cross-reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: powersums
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: powersums(f,b,i); f poly; b,i ideal. Return: list, the power sums of results of evaluating f at zeros of I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: i is a Groebner basis and b is an ordered monomial basis of r/i. Example with V(I) containing two points demonstrates the powersums returned. See symmfunc cross-reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: symmfunc
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: symmfunc(s); s list. Return: list, the symmetric functions of roots of a polynomial given power sums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows computing symmetric function coefficients from power sums and comparing to polynomial coefficients. See powersums cross-reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: univarpoly
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: univarpoly(l); l list. Return: poly, p on first variable of basering with coefficients from list l (p = l[1] + l[2]*x + ...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example constructs polynomial from list [1,2,3,4,5] yielding x^4+2x^3+3x^2+4x+5.

rubrics_metrics.name: qbase
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: qbase(I); I zero-dimensional ideal. Return: ideal, a monomial basis of quotient between basering and I, sorted by basering order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example compares qbase(i) with kbase(i) outputs. See Section 5.1.67 [kbase] for related routine. Assumes i has been standard-basis processed (std).

rubrics_metrics.name: isuni
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isuni(p); poly p. Return: poly, the variable if p is univariate; otherwise zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows isuni returns x for a univariate polynomial and 0 otherwise. See whichvariable for related check.

rubrics_metrics.name: whichvariable
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: whichvariable(p); poly p. Return: poly, the variable if p is a univariate monomial, otherwise 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: p is a monomial. Examples show whichvariable(x^5) -> x, whichvariable(x^3*y) -> 0. Cross-reference isuni.

rubrics_metrics.name: varsigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: varsigns(l); list l. Return: int, the number of sign changes in list l.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show varsigns([1,2,3]) -> 0 and varsigns([1,-1,2,-2,3,-3]) -> 5. See boundposDes cross-reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: boundBuFou
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: boundBuFou(p,a,b); p poly, a,b number. Return: int, an upper bound for number of real roots of p in (a,b] (with same parity as actual number) using the Budan-Fourier Theorem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: p univariate with rational coefficients, a<b rational. Examples show behavior on sample polynomial. See boundposDes and varsigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: boundposDes
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: boundposDes(p); poly p. Return: int, an upper bound for number of positive roots of p with same parity as actual number (Descartes' rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: p univariate with rational coefficients. Examples demonstrate increase when polynomial is multiplied by x^2+1. Cross-reference boundBuFou and boundDes.

rubrics_metrics.name: boundDes
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: boundDes(p); poly p. Return: int, an upper bound for the number of real roots of p with same parity as actual number (Descartes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: p univariate with rational coefficients. Examples show effect of multiplying by x^2+1. Cross-reference boundBuFou.

rubrics_metrics.name: allrealst
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: allrealst(p); poly p. Return: int: 1 iff all roots of p are real, checked via Sturm's Theorem; otherwise 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: p univariate with rational coefficients. Example shows polynomial with only real roots returns 1, after multiplying by x^2+1 returns 0. See allreal and sturm/sturmha.

rubrics_metrics.name: maxabs
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: maxabs(p); poly p. Return: number, an upper bound for largest absolute value of a root of p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: p univariate with rational coefficients. Example returns 11 for sample polynomial. See sturm cross-reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: allreal
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: allreal(p); Return: int, 1 iff all roots of p are real, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided. Cross-references allrealst and sturm.

rubrics_metrics.name: sturm
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sturm(p,a,b); poly p, number a,b. Return: int, the number of real roots of p in (a,b].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: p univariate with rational coefficients, a<b rational. Examples demonstrate counting real roots, including when polynomial is multiplied by quadratic factors. See sturmseq, sturmha, allreal.

rubrics_metrics.name: sturmseq
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sturmseq(p); p poly. Return: list, a Sturm sequence of p (remainder sequence starting with p, p' and continuing with negatives of remainders).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: p univariate with rational coefficients. Theory reference to Basu, Pollack, Roy. Example shows generated sequence polynomials. See sturmhaseq.

rubrics_metrics.name: sturmha
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sturmha(p,a,b); poly p, number a,b. Return: int, number of real roots of p in (a,b) using a Sturm-Habicht sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given; cross-references to sturm and sturmhaseq. Useful when Sturm-Habicht sequence has better coefficient-size behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: sturmhaseq
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sturmhaseq(P); P poly. Return: list, non-zero polynomials of the Sturm-Habicht (subresultant) sequence of P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: P univariate polynomial. Theory: Sturm-Habicht sequence defined via subresultants; behaves better for coefficient size. Example prints sequence; cross-references sturm, sturmha, sturmseq.

rubrics_metrics.name: reverse
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: reverse(l); l list. Return: list, l reversed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple utility; example shows reversing list [1,2,3,4,5] -> [5,4,3,2,1]. Cross-reference: used in other sequence manipulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: nrroots
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: nrroots(p); poly p. Return: int, the number of real roots of p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates counting real roots; cross-references boundposDes, sturm, sturmha. Assumes p univariate with rational coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: isparam
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isparam(ideal/module/poly/list); Return: int, 0 if argument has non-parametric coefficients and 1 if it has parametric coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples demonstrate behavior in different rings with parameters. Useful for distinguishing parametric vs numeric inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: fullSpace
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: fullSpace(n); n int. Return: cone, the ambient space of dimension n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: fullSpace(2) returns cone with lineality generators for ambient 2-space. Part of gfan.lib interface to gfan/gfanlib for convex geometry computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: origin(n); n int. Return: cone, the origin in ambient space of dimension n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows origin(2) and its equations. gfan interface routine.

rubrics_metrics.name: positiveOrthant
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: positiveOrthant(n); n int. Return: cone, the positive orthant of dimension n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows rays for positiveOrthant(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: ambientDimension
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ambientDimension(c/f/p); c cone, f fan, p polytope. Return: int, dimension of ambient space of the input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show ambientDimension for cones, fans, polytopes. Useful to check embedding dimension of objects created via gfan routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: canonicalizeCone
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: canonicalizeCone(c); c cone. Return: cone, a unique representation of cone c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute unique representation (facets, lineality) to make outputs comparable. Example compares c and canonicalized cc and shows equality. Note: bring cone to canonical form before calling procedures that assume unique representation; relativeInteriorPoint example.

rubrics_metrics.name: codimension
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: codimension(c/f/p); c cone, f fan, p polytope. Return: int, the codimension of input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples demonstrate codimension for cones and fans; codimension(fan) returns -1 for empty fan, then updates with inserted cones. Use to query combinatorial dimension info.

rubrics_metrics.name: coneViaPoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: coneViaPoints(HL); coneViaPoints(HL,L); coneViaPoints(HL,L,flags). Return: cone generated by half-lines (rows of HL) and optionally lines (rows of L).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flags (0..3) control whether HL rows are assumed rays (upper bit) and whether span of L is lineality space (lower bit); if bits are 0 program computes info itself. Examples show cones with lineality, facets, and how to supply L and flags to avoid recomputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: coneViaInequalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: coneViaInequalities(IE); coneViaInequalities(IE,E); coneViaInequalities(IE,E,flags). Return: cone consisting of all x such that IE*x >= 0 and E*x = 0 (if given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inequalities and equations are transformed to remove redundancies. Flags similar to coneViaPoints: upper bit assumes each inequality yields a facet, lower bit assumes kernel of E is span of cone; if bits 0 program computes info. Examples illustrate how to pass IE and E and flags to control assumptions; output shows inequalities and lineality.

rubrics_metrics.name: coneLink
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: coneLink(c,w); c cone, w intvec/bigintmat. Return: cone, the link of c around w.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example computing coneLink and printing rays and lineality. Useful for local combinatorial operations around a given vector.

rubrics_metrics.name: containsAsFace
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: containsAsFace(c,d); c cone, d cone. Return: 1 if d is a face of c; 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates difference between containsInSupport (point in support) and containsAsFace (face relation).

rubrics_metrics.name: containsInSupport
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: containsInSupport(c,d) or containsInSupport(c,p); c cone, d cone, p intvec. Return: 1 if d or p is contained in c; 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show containment tests for cones and points. Useful for geometric inclusion tests in gfan.

rubrics_metrics.name: containsPositiveVector
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: containsPositiveVector(c); c cone. Return: 1 if c contains a vector with only positive entries in its relative interior; 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show cones that do and do not contain positive interior vectors. Useful as a quick combinatorial test for positivity properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: containsRelatively
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: containsRelatively(c,p); c cone, intvec p. Return: 1 iff the cone contains the point in its relative interior; 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates checks for interior vs boundary membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: convexHull
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: convexHull(c1,c2) or convexHull with combinations of cone/polytopes. Return: convex hull of inputs (cone or polytope as appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports convexHull of cone-cone, cone-polytope, polytope-cone, polytope-polytope. Example header present; used for combining geometric objects in gfan computations.
